Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with a wrist injury diagnosed as a distal radius fracture. The
mechanism of injury, a moderate-speed rear impact with airbag deployment, is consistent with the injury sustained. Over the
cousre of 15 visits, the patient received immobilization, serial radiographs showing progressive callus formation, occupational
therapy focused on range of motion and grip strengthening, and monitoring for complications. The recovery timeline was
somewhat longer than typically expected for this fracture pattern, attributed to stiffness and a slower return of grip strength.
Physical examination documented tenderness over the fracture site, reduced wrist flexion and extension, and decreased grip
strength on the injured side, while neurovascular testing and sensation remained within normal limits. The patient reports no prior
injury or treatment to the affected wrist or forearm. Billing records reflect single charges for each service rendered, with no
duplicated or repeated entries. Current prognosis is guarded but improving, with continued therapy and a follow-up evaluation
planned.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
